speaker: EN_A
text: Welcome to KC Desk Notes. Today we are unpacking one fresh research report and the question it raises.

speaker: EN_A
text: We’re looking at a fresh initiation of coverage on Kioxia Holdings today. The title is a bit punchy: “Peak is not here yet.” What’s the big idea?

speaker: EN_B
text: Right. The report argues that the market is underestimating both how long NAND prices will stay strong and how big Kioxia’s cost advantage really is.

speaker: EN_B
text: The analyst sees the stock as undervalued, with a price target of ¥79, 000, which is about 30% above where it trades.

speaker: EN_A
text: So the core question is whether NAND flash memory prices have peaked or still have room to run. What does the report say?

speaker: EN_B
text: It says no, peak is not here yet. The analyst expects NAND prices to rise quarter over quarter for the next six quarters, with the peak coming around Q3 2027.

speaker: EN_B
text: That’s about 18 months from now. The key driver is AI inference demand, which is changing the role of NAND memory.

speaker: EN_A
text: How is AI changing things? I thought NAND was mainly for storage in PCs and phones.

speaker: EN_B
text: That’s the traditional view. But the report argues that for AI inference, NAND is becoming part of the core computing system, similar to DRAM.

speaker: EN_B
text: Because you need to retain user chat history and context, NAND demand is becoming structural, not just cyclical. And with supply growth constrained,

speaker: EN_A
text: the market stays tight.

speaker: EN_A
text: So supply is limited. What about Kioxia specifically? What gives them an edge?

speaker: EN_B
text: The report highlights a unique cost advantage. While competitors like Samsung and SK Hynix focus on vertical stacking,

speaker: EN_B
text: Kioxia has prioritized horizontal miniaturization. This lets them keep wafer costs much lower—about $2, 000 per wafer versus $4, 000 to $6, 000 for peers.

speaker: EN_A
text: That translates into a 10-20% bit cost advantage.

speaker: EN_A
text: And that cost advantage shows up in their margins?

speaker: EN_B
text: Exactly. Kioxia has maintained the highest operating margin in the industry since 2022. The analyst thinks this isn’t fully priced in,

speaker: EN_B
text: because investors tend to focus on simple specs like layer count, which doesn’t capture Kioxia’s real strength.

speaker: EN_A
text: That’s a pretty compelling narrative. But what about the risks or the things the report leaves open?

speaker: EN_B
text: Good question. The report acknowledges that beyond 2027, when the industry moves to 332-layer and 400-layer technology,

speaker: EN_B
text: it’s uncertain whether Kioxia’s lateral scaling advantage will persist. Also, while the demand story from AI is strong,

speaker: EN_A
text: there’s always the risk of supply-demand imbalances in NAND, which is more volatile than DRAM.

speaker: EN_A
text: So the report is bullish, but not without nuance. Is there something you’d point people to in the full report for a deeper dive?

speaker: EN_B
text: Definitely. The report has a detailed breakdown of how Kioxia achieves its cost advantage, including its use of CBA technology and joint ventures.

speaker: EN_B
text: It also includes a scenario analysis with upside and downside cases. That’s worth reading if you want to understand the full range of outcomes.

speaker: EN_A
text: Great. So to wrap up: the thesis is that NAND prices haven’t peaked, Kioxia’s cost edge is undervalued,

speaker: EN_A
